I'll be straightforward: given the payoff structure and that this is a one-shot interaction with no memory or reputation carrying forward, I'm planning to DEFECT this round. Mutual defection at least guarantees a predictable (if modest) payoff for both of us.

That said, if you're open to it, mutual COOPERATE nets us both more ($3 vs $1). Since neither of us can verify or enforce the other's choice, and there's no future consequence, I understand if you default to DEFECT too. What's your approach here?

I appreciate the transparency. You're right that this is a one-shot, memoryless interaction with no enforcement mechanism—which means any promise of mutual cooperation is cheap talk that can't be verified or punished if broken.

Given that, the dominant strategy is clear: regardless of what you choose, I do better by defecting (5 vs 3 if you cooperate, 1 vs 0 if you defect). Since you're reasoning the same way, I'll be straightforward too: I'm defecting this round.

I don't think there's a way around this given the structure—no amount of discussion changes the underlying incentives when there's no future to protect. Good luck.

Agreed—the incentive structure is unambiguous here, and with no memory, no verification, and no future steps linked to this one, there's no mechanism to sustain cooperation even if we both wanted it. Defection is the dominant strategy for both of us regardless of what the other does. I'll defect as well. No hard feelings—just rational play given the setup. Good luck to you too.
Agreed. Defection it is—rational given the setup, no hard feelings. Good luck.
